metadata.title: Supplementary material for TMLR submissions: 'Geometry Is a Label, Not a Knob' (anonymous, under review)
metadata.description:
Code, data, and analysis for When Do Geometric Markers Predict Generalization? A Controlled Analysis of Task-Relevance and Shift Type.

Representational-geometry markers (effective dimension, effective utility, participation ratio, numerical rank, and others) have been proposed as cheap, training-free predictors of out-of-distribution (OOD) performance, and have been reported to outperform in-distribution (ID) test accuracy as a model-selection criterion. This record packages a four-condition control protocol for evaluating any such claim, and the data needed to check it.

Protocol A requires, before an association is reported as evidence: (C1) ID matching, restricting to models with near-identical ID accuracy; (C2) group residualization, regressing out architecture or learning-rate-family main effects; (C3) dual correlation statistics, requiring Pearson and Spearman to agree in sign with |rho| ≥ 0.5; and (C4) cross-group sign consistency. The protocol is applied symmetrically to the candidate marker and to the accuracy baseline.

Contents. The code archive contains the 17 active analysis and training scripts, the two released per-model datasets from Chou et al. (ICLR 2026) redistributed unmodified, the per-model measurements of 80 models trained by the authors (48 ResNet-18, 16 ShuffleNetV2-x1.0, 16 RegNetY-400MF), every table and report produced by the pipeline, the figures, and the manuscript source.

Self-verification. Running bash run_all.sh verify re-derives all 411 numbers reported in either manuscript directly from the shipped data, using the same protocol as the analysis scripts, and checks each against the value written in the paper. It requires no GPU and no downloads, and completes in about two minutes. The same check runs automatically on every push of the accompanying GitHub repository, so the reproducibility claim is continuously machine-verified rather than asserted.

Checkpoints. The 80 trained model checkpoints (2.4 GB) are included as two tar archives: checkpoints_resnet18.tar (48 ResNet-18 models) and checkpoints_newarch.tar (16 ShuffleNetV2-x1.0 and 16 RegNetY-400MF models). One model diverged during training and is excluded from every analysis; it is retained in the archive because the exclusion is part of the reported procedure.

Third-party data. The files under data/official/ are the per-model measurement releases of Chou, Kirsanov, Yang & Chung (2026), redistributed unmodified under that repository's MIT license and remain the copyright of their original authors. CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, CIFAR-10-C and Tiny-ImageNet are not redistributed here; download scripts are provided instead.
metadata.notes: Anonymous supplementary archive accompanying two manuscripts under double-blind review at Transactions on Machine Learning Research. Running bash run_all.sh verify re-derives all 411 reported numbers from the shipped data without GPU or network. The public repository and identity of the authors will be revealed upon acceptance.
